segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, so Quickline came back on the renewal. They want 62 seats for another 12 months, start date February 1, and they asked if we can hold the 6% uplift instead of 8%.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: That should be inside the band. What’s the annual coming out to?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: $78,360 before tax, same support tier. To get the extension ready, I had to enter the 62 seats, February 1 start date, uplift, PO requirement, and billing contact in the quote tool, contract workspace, approval portal, billing tool, and the proposal template; it took most of yesterday and this morning, but the packet is clean now.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Okay, good. Did legal change anything material in the extension?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: No, just updated the term dates and left the limitation language as-is. Their procurement person, Dana, was mostly looking for net 30 and the invoice split by department.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: And we can do the split, right, 40 seats under operations and 22 under customer care?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yep. First invoice on February 3, then annual after that. I noted both cost centers in the order summary.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Great. Send it to Dana and copy their VP. If they sign by Friday, we’ll keep the February 1 go-live clean.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yep, I’m sending it after this. I’ll also give them the direct support email so they don’t route setup questions back through us.
